facts.statement: Before its formal description in 2011, the animal was referred to as the "Fruita form".
facts.quote: Before it was formally described in 2011, it was also known as the "Fruita form".

facts.statement: The first remains of Fruitachampsa were discovered by paleontologists James Clark and George Callison in 1975.
facts.quote: The first remains of Fruitachampsa were found by paleontologists James Clark and George Callison in 1975

facts.statement: The species was formally described by James Clark in 2011, naming it Fruitachampsa callisoni to honor George Callison.
facts.quote: Fruitachampsa callisoni was formally described by James Clark in 2011, with the specific name honoring George Callison.

facts.statement: This animal lived during the Upper Jurassic period in the Morrison Formation of Colorado.
facts.quote: Fruitachampsa is a genus of shartegosuchid crocodyliform from the Upper Jurassic Morrison Formation of Colorado.

facts.statement: Fruitachampsa lived between 152.21 and 143.1 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: It was a small, terrestrial quadrupedal predator under 1 meter long with a short face and prominent canine-like teeth in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: It is known from multiple specimens that show it to have been a relatively long-limbed terrestrial quadrupedal predator less than 1 m long, with a short face and a prominent pair of canine-like teeth in the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Although it was under 1 meter long, its 9 cm skull made it larger than other shartegosuchids.
facts.quote: It is a small crocodyliform under 1 m in length. Although small, Fruitachampsa is large in comparison to other shartegosuchids, with a maximum skull length of 9 cm.

facts.statement: Unlike other crocodyliforms, this animal lacked holes in its lower jaw and in front of its eye sockets.
facts.quote: Unlike other crocodyliforms, Fruitachampsa lacks mandibular or antorbital fenestrae (holes in the lower jaw and in front of the eye sockets).

facts.statement: As a terrestrial predator, it possessed long and extremely slender limbs.
facts.quote: As a terrestrial crocodyliform, Fruitachampsa has long and extremely slender limbs.

facts.statement: Its back was covered by two overlapping rows of bony plates called osteoderms, which were much thinner than those of modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Bony plates called osteoderms cover the back in two overlapping rows, and are much thinner than those of living crocodylians.

facts.statement: It is the only known shartegosuchid from North America and represents one of the youngest members of this group.
facts.quote: Fruitachampsa is the only shartegosuchid known from North America, and is one of the youngest members of the group.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the presence of Fruitachampsa indicates shartegosuchids migrated from Asia into North America via Europe during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The presence of Fruitachampsa in the western United States suggests that shartegosuchids radiated from Asia into North America.
